bib.title: Large Language Models are Few-shot Testers: Exploring LLM-based General Bug Reproduction

question: Can an LLM prompted with a bug report generate bug reproducing tests for general (non-crash) bugs, and can post-processing tell when to trust them?
hypothesis: Prompting Codex with a bug report, then executing, clustering and ranking its sampled tests, reproduces a substantial share of bugs and flags the reliable ones.
contributions: An analysis of open source repositories to verify the importance of generating bug reproducing test cases from bug reports
A framework (LIBRO) to harness an LLM to reproduce bugs, and suggest generated tests to the developer only when the results are reliable
Extensive empirical analyses on two datasets (Defects4J and the new GHRB)

method.summary: LIBRO builds a Markdown prompt from the bug report (optionally with example report-test pairs), samples tests from Codex at temperature 0.7, injects each into the lexically closest existing test class and resolves imports, runs them on the buggy program, clusters failing tests by failure output, and ranks them by report match, cluster size and test length. Selection shows results only if the largest failure cluster exceeds a threshold.
method.task: bug report to bug-reproducing test generation (Java, JUnit)

datasets.name: Defects4J 2.0 (with bug reports)
datasets.size: 750 bugs (814 with a paired report; 58 incorrect pairings and 6 differing directory structures removed)
datasets.split: all 750 evaluated; 60 bugs overlap JCrashPack for crash-tool comparison
datasets.source: 17 Java projects; Chart has only 8 reports

datasets.name: GHRB (GitHub Recent Bugs)
datasets.split: 581 PRs after Codex cutoff -> 435 adding tests -> 84 merged, single-issue -> 31 where developer test fails pre-merge and passes post-merge
datasets.source: 17 GitHub JUnit repositories; PRs created after Codex training cutoff (July 2021)

datasets.name: Java-med (test-addition mining study)
datasets.size: 1000 top-starred Java projects; 970 cloned, 550 with JUnit, 300 with issue-referencing test-adding commit
datasets.preprocessing: test-adding commit = diff adds @Test with body; issue link = 'fixes/resolves/closes #NUM' or PR mentioning an issue

models.name: Codex code-davinci-002
models.architecture: GPT-3 fine-tuned on source code (per the paper)

models.name: Copy&Paste
models.architecture: uses code snippets from the report (HTML pre tag or infoZilla) as the test

inference.decoding: sampling; generation stops at first closing code fence
inference.samples: n=50 tests per bug in the default setting (two examples); n=10 settings for ablations; 1000 resamples for query-count simulation; random ranking baseline averaged over 100 runs
inference.prompting: Markdown document from report title and description, then 'Provide a self-contained example that reproduces this issue', an opening code fence and 'public void test'; default uses two handpicked report-test pairs (Time-24, Lang-1) for all projects; within-project variant uses oldest tests in project

parameters.agreement_threshold_Thr: 1 for main results (350 of 570 FIB bugs selected); 10 as aggressive value
parameters.ranking_order: report-output match, then output cluster size, then token count; round-robin across clusters

other.env: Ubuntu 18.04.6, 32GB RAM, Intel i7-7700 3.60GHz, Python 3.9, javalang parser

metrics.name: reproduced bugs
metrics.definition: bugs with at least one test that fails on the buggy version and passes on the fixed version (BRT)

metrics.name: acc@n
metrics.definition: number of bugs whose BRT is within top n ranked tests; precision = acc@n / selected bugs

metrics.name: wef@n
metrics.definition: number of non-reproducing tests ranked above any BRT (total FIB count if none); wef@n over top n

metrics.name: FIB
metrics.definition: tests that compile and fail in the buggy program

eval.protocol: Defects4J uses PRE_FIX/POST_FIX revisions; GHRB uses pre/post-merge. EvoCrash judged under same BRT criterion. No significance test stated; single Codex run set per setting.

prompts.purpose: instruction line of the LIBRO prompt; full template: Markdown title/description, '## Reproduction', this line as blockquote, an opening code fence, then 'public void test' (Listing 1)
prompts.text: Provide a self-contained example that reproduces this issue.

results.claim: LIBRO reproduces 251 of 750 Defects4J bugs under the default two-example n=50 setting.
results.setup: Defects4J 2.0, Codex code-davinci-002, temperature 0.7, 50 samples, two handpicked examples
results.quote: we find that overall 251 bugs, or 33.5% of 750 studied Defects4J bugs, are reproduced by LIBRO

results.claim: On the 31-bug post-cutoff GHRB set LIBRO reproduces 10 bugs.
results.quote: LIBRO can automatically generate bug reproducing tests for 10 bugs based on 50 trials, for a success rate of 32.2%

results.claim: Top-1 ranked test reproduces the bug for 149 bugs, versus 116 for random ranking.
results.table: Table VI, row n=1, column Defects4J acc@n LIBRO

results.claim: Selection at Thr=1 picks 350 of 570 FIB bugs, 219 reproduced: precision 0.63, recall 0.87.
results.quote: Among the 570 bugs with a FIB, 350 bugs are selected.

results.claim: Raising the threshold to 10 gives precision 0.84 at recall 0.42.
results.quote: we can achieve a higher precision of 0.84 for a recall of 0.42

results.claim: Two examples (n=50) reproduce 251 bugs; no-example n=10 reproduces 124 and two-example n=10 median 173.
results.setup: Defects4J, n=10 samples per bug, no example
results.table: Table III, row No Example (n=10), column reproduced
results.note: n=10 and n=50 rows differ in query count as well as examples

results.claim: A within-project example performs worse than a generic example because Codex copies it.
results.table: Table III, row One Example from Source Project (n=10), column reproduced
results.note: baseline is the One Example (n=10) row, 166

results.claim: Reproduced bugs grow logarithmically with the number of generated tests with no plateau.
results.setup: Defects4J, 1000 resamples from 50 tests per bug
results.quote: The number of bugs reproduced increases logarithmically to the number of tests generated, with no sign of performance plateauing.

results.claim: Stack traces help crash bugs, 84 versus 69 reproduced with one example.
results.setup: Defects4J crash bugs, one example, n=10
results.table: Table III, row One Example with Stack, Crash Bugs (n=10), column reproduced

results.claim: LIBRO reproduces 91 more unique bugs than EvoCrash (19 crash bugs).
results.setup: JCrashPack and Defects4J overlap (60 bugs), BRT criterion
results.quote: LIBRO reproduced 91 more unique bugs (19 being crash bugs) than EvoCrash

results.claim: A 50-test run takes 444 s in total, 292 s of it API querying.
results.setup: 50 tests per bug on i7-7700 machine
results.quote: LIBRO took an average of 444 seconds to generate 50 tests and process them

results.claim: Median 28.4% ratio of tests added by issue-referencing commits to current suite size.
results.setup: 300 Java repositories from Java-med, Aug 2022 suite size
results.quote: is 28.4%, suggesting that a significant number of tests are added due to bug reports
results.note: Abstract says about 28%; paper says this is not the share of tests originating from reports

results.claim: 81% of tokens in generated tests overlap the report code snippets when snippets exist.
results.setup: Defects4J reports with any code snippet
results.quote: on average 81% of the tokens in the body of the LIBRO-generated test methods overlapped with the tokens in the code snippets

results.claim: Most common failure cause in 40 manually checked cases is missing helper definitions (13).
results.quote: happening in 13 cases, was a need of helper defini

limits: Codex has likely seen the Defects4J projects; GHRB has only 31 bugs.
Authors concede results may not generalise to other languages or to projects unlike the model's training data.
Does not work for tests that need external files or unusual test infrastructure (Checkstyle 0/13, Closure 2/172).
Codex code-davinci-002 is a closed beta model that has since been retired.
No variance or significance test beyond resampling; ablations use n=10 versus default n=50.

terms.definition: Bug Reproducing Test: a test that fails due to the bug specified in the report
Fail In the Buggy program: a test that compiles and fails in the buggy program
